slate.title: [ABSTRACT] "Adding one trace term per candidate removes the bias and restores complete-data-equivalent selection." — trace correction overstates decisions

[ABSTRACT] "Model selection on multiply imputed data is biased toward more complex models, because their larger relative increase in variance makes the fit look better than it is." — model-selection scope too broad
[S1-P4] "The practical consequence is that, for such a model, every deviance and every information criterion computed from multiply imputed data is too optimistic." — every-criterion sign overclaim

[S1-P6b] "Adding one term per candidate, the trace of its relative-increase-in-variance matrix, removes the bias and substantially restores the ranking that complete data would have given." — trace-only removal overclaim
[S1-P5] "The missing data have then destroyed part of the evidence in its favor, and we show that no transformation of the observed data can recover it." — unearned impossibility claim
[S1-P5] "Correction then restores complete-data behavior entirely." — entirely too strong
[S6-P7] "No transformation of the observed data manufactures the lost evidence back." — restates disclaimed impossibility
[S6-P1] "The bias exists only when the fit estimates a scale or covariance." — contradicted by known-scale MI
[S6-P7] "Corrected selection and calibrated tests behave as they would have with complete data." — decision equivalence too broad

[S6-P7b] "When the aim is to rank models or to compare nested models on imputed data, and no calibrated reference distribution already absorbs the bias, add the per-candidate trace correction before reading off the result." — nested-test correction conflation
[S1-P4] "A model-comparison table built on imputed data therefore favors the candidates with the most missing information." — deterministic ranking overclaim
[S6-P7] "Then trust the result the way complete-data results are trusted." — applied trust too broad
[S5-P22] "The bootstrap imputation sampler reproduces the analytic results on the most demanding cells, which bounds the cost of not running data augmentation." — empirical check not a bound
[S1-P4] "In our pre-registered study, every misclassification by uncorrected MI-AIC chose the candidate with the largest RIV."
[S5-P17] "This is a registered directional prediction, and it held across all sixty cells." — cell scope unclear
[S3-P6] "A derivation produced and checked within a single model family would likely have shipped one sign without noticing that there was a choice." — counterfactual workflow claim
[S1-P3] "The open questions above are open because the second and third levels had not been posed." — speculates on field history
[S1-P2] "Only one information criterion has been proposed for multiply imputed data." — ignores other cited criteria
[S5-P6] "By contrast, the Satorra-Bentler arm applies a scaled-and-shifted statistic referred to $\chi^2_1$." — missing test citation
[S6-P6] "De-shrinkage of estimated noncentrality and joint calibration of score vectors across candidates are developed separately." — points to missing reference
